sections.title: Performance Audit — Supaprod (verified against HEAD, uncommitted `loop.server.ts` diff is cosmetic only)
sections.content: Note: the components in your "Codebase Context" (`ranking.ts`, `format.ts`, `governance-shared.ts`, `decisions-shared.ts`, `incident-format.ts`, the ink/`Card`/`Input` components) are pure functions and presentational components already confirmed clean on a prior pass — no re-renders, no N+1, nothing to fix there. The real issues live in the server hooks and panel components below.

sections.title: 1. N+1 queries
2. Unnecessary re-renders (missing memoization)
3. Caching opportunities
4. Memory leaks
5. Redundant computation
sections.content:
**`src/lib/ai/loop.server.ts:825-859`** (`checkpoint`) — every step re-serializes the *entire* accumulated mission state (`conv`, `steps`, `approvalsQueued`, memories, etc.) into the `agent_run_checkpoints` upsert:
```ts
const checkpoint = async (stepIndex: number) => {
  await supabase.from("agent_run_checkpoints").upsert({
    run_id: runId, user_id: userId, workspace_id: workspaceId, step_index: stepIndex,
    state: { agent, workspaceId, model, traceId, goal: s.goal, conv, steps, approvalsQueued, ... },
  }, { onConflict: "run_id,step_index" });
  ...
};
```
Since `conv`/`steps` only grow, writing the full array every step means total write volume is O(n²) over an n-step run (step 1 writes 1 entry, step 2 writes 2, ... step n writes n). Fix — make checkpoints append-only: persist only the delta since the last checkpoint (or store `conv`/`steps` in a separate append-only table keyed by `(run_id, step_index)`), and reconstruct full state on resume by concatenating rows instead of storing the whole snapshot each time.
